subject: series
synopsis: The Phantom Stranger navigates divine missions while seeking his own redemption.
author: Dan DiDio

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries from the Ultimate Universe following a version of the Vision as a herald-like cosmic entity, connecting Ultimate mythology to larger galactic threats.
author: Mike Carey

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron and a roster of top artists' 2024 Disney special featuring Uncle Scrooge McDuck encountering a version of himself from another dimension — a metafictional love letter to Carl Barks' Duck stories that celebrates the character's publishing history while telling a genuinely clever story.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: Will Henry's warmhearted newspaper strip about a fearless boy and his friends exploring the New England coast in adventures that blend childhood imagination with authentic maritime atmosphere. A gently adventurous modern heir to the spirit of classic adventure strips.
author: Will Henry

subject: series
synopsis: An IDW collection of classic Walt Disney comics spanning decades of Mickey, Donald, and Goofy stories.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1988 series spinning out of the Legion of Super-Heroes, following a group of Legionnaire allies who have been transformed into new forms by an alien force. A short-lived tie-in that explored some interesting corners of DC's 30th-century universe.
author: Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2009 oversized anthology newspaper-format series featuring classic characters reimagined by top creator pairs including Neil Gaiman/Mike Allred on Metamorpho and Brian Azzarello/Eduardo Risso on Batman.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Wagner and Dan Schkade's 2015 Will Eisner's The Spirit: Ebony White and Commissioner Dolan search Central City for the Spirit after his two-year disappearance.
author: Matt Wagner

subject: series
synopsis: A four-issue anthology miniseries featuring backup stories spotlighting various X-Men in solo adventures, serving as a showcase for lesser-known mutants in shorter format stories.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2008 limited series by Christopher Yost focusing on Storm — her dual role as queen of Wakanda alongside T'Challa and as X-Man — as she faces a personal threat tied to both identities. One of Storm's better solo spotlights of the modern era.
author: Christopher Yost

subject: series
synopsis: Marc Guggenheim's post-ResurrXion X-Men series following Kitty Pryde leading a traditional X-Men team, deliberately evoking the classic Claremont era's tone while navigating modern mutant politics.
author: Marc Guggenheim

subject: series
synopsis: Jean Van Hamme's XIII Universe spinoff series — stories expanding the world of the amnesiac spy thriller, exploring characters from the original XIII saga in standalone adventures.
author: Jean Van Hamme

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Webtoon series: teenage Zatanna, touring with her father's magic act, is pulled into Victorian London and the hunt for Jack the Ripper.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's flagship title and one of the most beloved runs in comics. Lee/Ditko invented a new kind of hero; Conway killed Gwen Stacy; Michelinie/McFarlane defined the 90s look; Slott ran 100+ issues of intricate story. Essential reading.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Krueger and Alex Ross' twelve-issue limited series pits the modern Avengers and New Avengers against the WWII-era Invaders, accidentally transported to the present. Ross's lush painted covers complement a story that meditates on heroic idealism across generations.
author: Jim Krueger

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's original What If? (1977-1984): the Watcher narrates alternate outcomes of classic stories, such as Spider-Man joining the Fantastic Four or Phoenix surviving.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman and Esad Ribić's 2024 Aliens vs. Avengers: in a future overrun by Xenomorphs, the last aging Avengers make a final stand.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Aquaman's 1991 series: Arthur, having lost his wife, child and kingdom, throws himself into nonstop heroics; cancelled after 13 issues.
author: Peter David

subject: series
synopsis: Nathan Edmondson's 2014 series reimagining Deathlok as Henry Hayes, a schoolteacher who's been secretly programmed as a cyborg assassin without his knowledge, a fresh take on the concept with espionage thriller elements.
author: Nathan Edmondson

subject: series
synopsis: Thom Zahler's charming romantic comedy continues the domestic superhero saga of Abby and Mark following their marriage, dealing with the mundane and super in equal measure. One of the best examples of superhero-as-romantic-comedy genre, warm and genuinely funny.
author: Thom Zahler

subject: series
synopsis: Anna Marie's various solo series. The character works best as supporting player — extended solos struggle with the untouchability premise. Howard Mackie's original limited series is charming.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Benjamin Percy's Rebirth Teen Titans: Damian Wayne recruits Starfire, Raven, Beast Boy and Kid Flash, then Adam Glass's darker team.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jurgens' 1986 Booster Gold: a disgraced 25th-century football player travels back in time with stolen tech to become a corporate-sponsored hero.
author: Dan Jurgens, Lilah Sturges

subject: series
synopsis: Bruce Jones's 2006 Vertigo reimagining of Deadman: Brandon Cayce dies in a plane crash and wanders an eerie afterlife.
author: Bruce Jones

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and David Marquez's 2015 Invincible Iron Man: Tony Stark in new armor faces Madame Masque and a reformed Doctor Doom.
author: Matt Fraction, Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Keith Giffen, J.M. DeMatteis and Kevin Maguire's 1987 Justice League: the first six issues of the bwa-ha-ha era, before it became Justice League International.
author: J. M. DeMatteis, Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Top Cow's Witchblade: NYPD detective Sara Pezzini bonds with an ancient living gauntlet; files are mostly the 1995 run by Wohl, Christina Z and Michael Turner.
author: David Wohl, Christina Z

subject: series
synopsis: Harley Quinn's Rebirth series (2016-2020): Conner and Palmiotti's Coney Island antics continue, then Frank Tieri and Sam Humphries.
author: Jimmy Palmiotti, Amanda Conner

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Slott's 2014 Amazing Spider-Man: Peter Parker regains his body after Superior, launches Parker Industries and fights through Spider-Verse.

subject: series
synopsis: A Dynamite Comics Army of Darkness miniseries.
author: Mike Raicht, James Kuhoric

subject: series
synopsis: Heroes Reborn Avengers (1996-1997): Rob Liefeld and Jeph Loeb's 13-issue pocket-universe reboot.
author: Stan Lee, Bill Mantlo

subject: series
synopsis: Tony Isabella and Eddy Newell's 1995 Black Lightning: Jefferson Pierce returns to teach in Brick City's crumbling schools while fighting its gangs.
author: Jenny Blake Isabella, Dave Devries (Writer)

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker and Darwyn Cooke's 2002 Catwoman relaunch: Selina Kyle protects the East End with Holly and Slam Bradley, later Will Pfeifer's run.
author: Devin Grayson, Mary Jo Duffy

subject: series
synopsis: Francis Manapul and Brian Buccellato's New 52 The Flash: Barry Allen's visually inventive Speed Force adventures and revamped Rogues, later Robert Venditti.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's comic adaptation of X-Men: The Animated Series, second-season episodes.
author: Ralph Macchio, Mark Edens

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's comic adaptation of X-Men: The Animated Series, third-season episodes.
author: Ralph Macchio, Mark Edens

subject: series
synopsis: Sholly Fisch and Dario Brizuela's Batman & Scooby-Doo Mysteries: Mystery Inc. and the Dark Knight unmask fake monsters in Gotham.
author: Sholly Fisch, Ivan Cohen

subject: series
synopsis: Boom!'s original Adventure Time graphic novels: standalone Finn and Jake stories in the land of Ooo.
author: Ryan North, Christopher Hastings

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek and Cary Nord's 2004 Dark Horse Conan: a faithful, painterly return to Howard's young Cimmerian, from Hyperborea to Zamora.
author: Kurt Busiek, Robert E. Howard

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and Francis Manapul's 2010 Flash: Barry Allen back as a forensic scientist, the Renegades from the future and the lead-in to Flashpoint.

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid, Brian Augustyn and Barry Kitson's 1998 retelling of the Justice League's founding, with Black Canary, Flash, Green Lantern, Aquaman and J'onn as rookies.
author: Grant Morrison, Ruben Diaz

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's weekly Transformers (1984-1992): US reprints plus original Simon Furman stories, including Target: 2006 and the debut of Death's Head.

subject: series
synopsis: Kaoru Mori's meticulously researched historical manga following young bride Amir and her extended Central Asian family in the 19th century. A celebration of cultural customs, textile artistry, and quiet domestic life rendered in intricate, gorgeous detail.
author: Kaoru Mori

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages Spider-Man comic tied to the popular 1994 animated TV series, adapting and extending the show's storylines for younger readers. Faithful to the cartoon's simplified continuity and tone.
author: Nel Yomtov, Glenn Greenberg

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1986 continuation of the Outsiders following Batman's departure from the team. Writer Mike W. Barr maintained the team's dynamics — Black Lightning, Geo-Force, Katana, Halo, and Metamorpho — under new leadership.
author: Mike W. Barr

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's time-travel event featuring a future conquered by Ultron, leading Wolverine to travel back in time to kill Hank Pym before Ultron's creation. Stylish art from Bryan Hitch but a divisive, anticlimactic conclusion.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Hiroyuki's fast-paced four-panel gag manga follows the relationship between an incredibly stupid girl and the exhausted childhood friend who puts up with her. Extremely short-form but consistently funny in its one-note commitment to the premise.
author: Hiroyuki

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital companion to the Hunted storyline, following Spider-Man's conflict with Kraven the Hunter in a format optimized for mobile reading.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Faye Perozich and Daerick Gross' graphic novel adaptation of Anne Rice's bestselling novel — the vampire Lestat's origin story and his place in Rice's rich Vampire Chronicles mythology.
author: Faye Perozich

subject: series
synopsis: Jay Faerber and Nate Stockman's digital MonkeyBrain series in which a superhero and a supervillain swap bodies and must live each other's lives.
author: Jay Faerber

subject: series
synopsis: Shorter format Atomic Robo stories by various creators expanding the world of Brian Clevinger's beloved Tesla-built robot adventurer.
author: Brian Clevinger

subject: series
synopsis: A twelve-issue series reprinting the original Avengers issues with new framing sequences by various creators adding retrospective commentary. A pleasant way to revisit the early Avengers stories with editorial context.
author: Macon Blair, Dwayne McDuffie

subject: series
synopsis: A charming crossover between Adam West's Batman and the British spy duo from The Avengers TV series, playing both shows' distinctive period tones against each other with wit.
author: Ian Edginton

subject: series
synopsis: Kevin Smith, Ralph Garman, and Ty Templeton's affectionate crossover uniting the Adam West Batman with the Van Williams/Bruce Lee Green Hornet in period-faithful style. Captures the campy exuberance of both 1960s TV shows.
author: Kevin Smith

subject: series
synopsis: Marc Andreyko and Jeff Parker's crossover spanning from Batman's 1960s to Wonder Woman's 1970s setting, using the time gap as a storytelling device. A respectful celebration of both classic TV portrayals.
author: Marc Andreyko

subject: series
synopsis: Andrew Helfer's Batman limited series set in the early years of Bruce Wayne's career, exploring a period when his methods were still being defined. Atmospheric but underwhelming compared to other Year One-style stories.
author: Andrew Helfer

subject: series
synopsis: Kelly Sue DeConnick and Valentine De Landro's feminist science fiction series set in a dystopian future where women deemed 'non-compliant' are sent to an off-world prison planet, drawing on 1970s women-in-prison exploitation films as feminist allegory.
author: Kelly Sue DeConnick

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's mature-content anthology (1981–1983), featuring adult-oriented horror and fantasy stories by John Byrne, Bill Sienkiewicz, and others working outside the Comics Code in one of Marvel's most experimental publishing spaces.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Burns' twelve-issue graphic novel set in 1970s suburban Seattle follows teenagers afflicted by a sexually transmitted plague that causes strange mutations; a landmark of literary horror comics with Burns' precise black-and-white art creating an indelible atmosphere of dread and adolescent alienation.
author: Charles Burns

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring T'Challa as Black Panther in adventures formatted for the Marvel Unlimited vertical reading platform.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Ales Kot's experimental, trippy series following Bucky through the multiverse as a cosmic operative, featuring Langdon Foss's surreal art. Deliberately strange and divisive but creatively ambitious.
author: Ales Kot

subject: series
synopsis: An Image Comics superhero satire.

subject: series
synopsis: Richard Comely's Canadian superhero Captain Canuck — a patriotic Mountie-turned-hero — in both the classic 1970s-80s original series and the modern revival, representing the rare successful indigenous Canadian superhero comic tradition.
author: Richard Comely

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring Carol Danvers as Captain Marvel in episodic stories formatted for the Marvel Unlimited platform.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's adaptation of Ted Turner's environmentally themed animated series, following the Planeteers who summon Captain Planet to fight ecological villains. Earnest and message-driven, aimed squarely at children.
author: Barry Dutter, Ian Rimmer

subject: series
synopsis: D.C. Johnson's 1998 cult series following Cameron Chase, a DEO agent with a deep-seated hatred of superheroes who investigates metahuman threats, praised for its realistic take on a bureaucratic superhero world.
author: D.C. Johnson

subject: series
synopsis: John Francis Moore's underrated DC series following Walker Gabriel, an accidental time-traveler who inherited the original Chronos's time suit. A clever, character-driven sci-fi adventure cancelled before its time, with an inventive approach to time travel mechanics.
author: John Francis Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Frank Tieri's 6-issue Countdown tie-in uses the Extremists as a vehicle for political satire about a Monarch-allied supervillain team taking over a parallel Earth. Ambitious in concept but constrained by its tie-in obligations.
author: Frank Tieri

subject: series
synopsis: DC's ambitious round-robin writing experiment where each issue's creator left an impossible cliffhanger for the next to resolve. The chaotic result is more interesting as a historical artifact than as a coherent story — a collision of DC's entire hero roster with no authorial control.
author: Mark Evanier, Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: Donna Troy is resurrected as a New God and her origin is once again rewritten.
author: Phil Jimenez

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages series reimagining DC's iconic female heroes — Supergirl, Batgirl, Wonder Woman, Harley Quinn, Poison Ivy, and Katana — as students at Super Hero High School. Written by Shea Fontana with art by Yancey Labat, it tied into the popular animated franchise and offered a fresh, accessible entry point for younger readers.
author: Shea Fontana

subject: series
synopsis: David Lapham and Rafael Ortiz's Avatar series about Dan, a crude slacker who cannot be physically harmed, dragged into ever more violent scrapes.
author: David Lapham

subject: series
synopsis: Beka and Crip's Papercutz series about three girls at a dance school navigating friendship, competition, and the challenges of ballet training. A popular French series that translated well for the all-ages American market.
author: Beka

subject: series
synopsis: Mika Yamamori's shojo romance following Suzume, a country girl adjusting to Tokyo life who develops feelings for her homeroom teacher — navigating the complications of an impossible love while also building genuine friendship with a classmate who cares for her. A character-sensitive romance that earns its emotional moments.
author: Mika Yamamori

subject: series
synopsis: Inio Asano's science fiction slice-of-life follows two high school friends in a Tokyo under alien occupation that most people have simply accepted as normal. A bittersweet, formally ambitious work about friendship, mortality, and the apocalypse as background noise.
author: Inio Asano

subject: series
synopsis: Julie Doucet's groundbreaking autobiographical and surrealist alt-comics series, known for its raw feminist voice, confessional intimacy, and hallucinatory dream sequences.
author: Julie Doucet

subject: series
synopsis: Pierre Gabus and Romuald Reutimann's anthropomorphic noir: Michael, an elephant immigrant turned journalist, uncovers corruption and a masked vigilante in a sprawling 1950s-style city.

subject: series
synopsis: Titan/IDW's 11-issue series celebrating Doctor Who's 50th anniversary, with each issue following a different Doctor in standalone adventures, culminating in a story uniting them all. A loving tribute to the full scope of Doctor Who's history.
author: Scott & David Tipton

subject: series
synopsis: J.H. Williams III's visually stunning fantasy adventure in landscape format, following Hope Redhood — a thief with a magic key — through a world that blends genres including noir, fantasy, and science fiction in an ambitious, experimental layout.
author: J.H. Williams III

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series exploring the edges of the Venomverse multiverse with symbiote stories formatted for the Marvel Unlimited platform.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Max Bemis and Andrea Mutti's political horror-thriller follows an America that gradually embraces fascism after a charismatic pop star turns the country's anger into a movement.
author: Max Bemis

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David's Fallen Angel follows Lee, a mysterious and powerful woman in the corrupt city of Bette Noire, meting out judgment with a moral calculus that seems to shift between cases — a quietly acclaimed supernatural crime drama.
author: Peter David

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series following the Super Young Team, a group of Japanese celebrity heroes, as they navigate fame and purpose in the wake of Final Crisis. Written by Joe Casey with art by ChrisCross.
author: Joe Casey

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series written by Ivan Brandon featuring Agent Chase of the DCU and Nemesis trapped in a surreal psychological facility called OMAC. A deliberately disorienting and unusual tie-in.
author: Ivan Brandon

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series following the villain-turned-hero Tattooed Man as he tries to protect his family in Liberty Hill while carrying the power of the Mark of Cain he received during Final Crisis. Written by Eric Wallace.
author: Eric Wallace

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series following the Human Flame, the relatively obscure villain who killed the Martian Manhunter, as he attempts to stay alive after Final Crisis while everyone wants him dead. Written by Matt Sturges.
author: Matt Sturges

subject: series
synopsis: A sequel crossover pitting Freddy Krueger, Jason Voorhees, and Ash Williams against a new army of nightmare warriors.

subject: series
synopsis: Jiro Matsumoto's disturbing noir manga is set in a Japan where revenge killing is legalized through an 'eye for an eye' system, following a mentally unstable proxy killer hired to carry out sanctioned murders. Dark, surreal, and blackly comic.
author: Jiro Matsumoto

subject: series
synopsis: Natsuki Takaya's shojo classic follows orphaned Tohru Honda who discovers her host family is cursed to transform into zodiac animals. A beautifully told story of trauma, healing, and unconditional acceptance that defined a generation of shojo readers.
author: Natsuki Takaya

subject: series
synopsis: Collected editions of the America's Elite era G.I. Joe stories, following the team in modern post-9/11 military contexts. An attempt to update the classic property for contemporary readers with generally solid results.
author: Mark Powers

subject: series
synopsis: Sergio Aragonés and Mark Evanier's Groo continuation spotlighting recurring characters from the long-running series in dedicated story arcs.
author: Sergio Aragonés

subject: series
synopsis: Gianluca Panniello's European western series published in English by Magnetic Press blends pulp western action with post-apocalyptic world-building, following a gunfighter through a transformed frontier. Strong genre craftsmanship and ambitious visual storytelling in the tradition of Italian western comics.
author: Gianluca Panniello

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024-2025 DC series following Harley Quinn in a standalone adventure setting her apart from the Gotham status quo, exploring what happens when the most chaotic character in DC encounters an equally unpredictable new environment.
author: C. R. C. Payne

subject: series
synopsis: Avatar Press's superhero satire series about the modern celebrity culture of superheroes, following a fan who gets close to his idol. A minor Ellis-adjacent entry in the Avatar catalog.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis' 2005 Marvel X-Men event where the Scarlet Witch's mental breakdown reshapes reality into a world ruled by Magneto and his mutant family — and the X-Men and Avengers must decide whether to restore the world knowing what it will cost. The 'No more mutants' conclusion permanently changed the Marvel universe.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Bubble Comics' superhero series following Igor Grom, St. Petersburg's most formidable detective, tackling supervillains and organized crime in Russia's first major domestic superhero franchise.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Image Comics' 30th anniversary anthology collecting original short stories from the publisher's roster of creator-owned talent. A showcase of the diversity and vitality of creator-owned comics from the publisher that redefined the industry.
author: Brenden Fletcher, Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Milligan and Max Fiumara's 2007 Infinity Inc.: Steel and others empowered by Lex Luthor's Everyman Project struggle with identity in a surreal, psychological take.
author: Peter Milligan, Dann Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Keith Giffen and Dan DiDio's New 52 revival of Jack Kirby's Fourth World characters, reimagining the Forever People as New Genesis teenagers given new modern identities on Earth. Ambitious but unable to fully leverage Kirby's mythology in a compressed 12-issue run.
author: Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: Oni Press's comic continuation of Jhonen Vasquez's beloved Nickelodeon series, with the original creative team bringing back Zim's idiotic alien invasion plots and Dib's frantic resistance. Captures the show's anarchic, ugly-cute aesthetic and nihilistic humor faithfully.
author: Jhonen Vasquez

subject: series
synopsis: A spin-off series set in Robert Kirkman's Invincible universe, focusing on supporting characters and secondary heroes navigating the aftermath of major crossover events in that world.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: DC limited series placing the Golden Age Justice Society in newly discovered wartime adventures, expanding the mythology of the heroes who preceded the Silver Age.
author: Kevin J. Anderson

subject: series
synopsis: Justin Gray and Jimmy Palmiotti's acclaimed 2006 Western series featuring the scarred Confederate bounty hunter Jonah Hex in mostly standalone stories, praised for its brutal, morally complex Western action.
author: Justin Gray, Jimmy Palmiotti

subject: series
synopsis: Naoya Matsumoto's breakout action series follows Kafka Hibino, who transforms into a powerful Kaiju-human hybrid while working in the anti-Kaiju Defense Force he once dreamed of joining. Extremely popular for its dynamic action sequences and likeable protagonist.
author: Naoya Matsumoto

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar's 2018 Kick-Ass relaunch: Patience Lee, an Army veteran and single mother, takes the suit to rob gangsters in New Mexico; later Steve Niles.
author: Mark Millar, Steve Niles

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen's licensed Lady Death limited series setting the character in a medieval fantasy world, adapting the Brian Pulido character for a more narrative-focused treatment at a mainstream publisher. Mediocre execution of an interesting premise.
author: Brian Pulido

subject: series
synopsis: Erica Schultz's 2024 series from Marvel's From the Ashes era following X-23/Laura Kinney as she takes on the Wolverine name and legacy in the post-Krakoa world, rebuilding her identity while navigating the changed landscape for mutants.
author: Erica Schultz

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue crossover event by John Ostrander and Len Wein that introduced a new Suicide Squad and the new Flash (Wally West as full Flash), as Darkseid manipulates public opinion against Earth's heroes. It served as the foundation for the post-Crisis DC universe's hero landscape.
author: John Ostrander, Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: Kentaro Sato's ultra-violent horror manga sees magical girl invaders wipe out most of humanity while survivors struggle to fight back. Deliberately provocative and gratuitously gory, functioning as a nihilistic deconstruction of the magical girl genre.
author: Kentaro Sato

subject: series
synopsis: Bubble Comics' companion series to Igor Grom, providing additional adventures for the Russian superhero detective who became the basis for the Netflix adaptation. A significant milestone in Russian comics publishing.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Roger Stern and John Byrne's clever 12-issue series depicting a team of Marvel heroes who operated in the gaps between the classic era and the modern age — told in reverse chronological order, with issue #12 released first. A love letter to Marvel history.
author: Roger Stern

subject: series
synopsis: IDW Publishing's all-ages Avengers series brought the team to younger readers with accessible storytelling and bright, clean artwork. A reliable entry point for new comic readers without prior Marvel knowledge, written with affection for the characters even if the stories lack the complexity of the main Marvel titles.
author: Matthew K. Manning

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages Spider-Man series from IDW Publishing (under Marvel Action imprint) designed for young readers, presenting kid-friendly adventures of Peter Parker that are accessible without prior Marvel knowledge and suitable for middle-grade audiences.
author: Delilah S. Dawson, Erik Burnham

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages retelling of classic Fantastic Four stories, companion to the Marvel Age Spider-Man anthology. Updated art and dialogue make Lee and Kirby's originals accessible for younger readers.
author: Stan Lee, Jack Kirby

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's lighthearted Infinity Comics series about the dogs of the Marvel universe in humorous adventures, featuring Lucky the Pizza Dog and other Marvel canines.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's companion comics to the Avengers Assemble: Ultron Revolution animated season, featuring stories set in the animated universe featuring the Ultron threat.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages adaptation of the Ultimate Spider-Man animated series' Web Warriors era, featuring Miles Morales, Spider-Gwen, and multiple Spider-characters in the all-ages animated style. A solid children's series built around the multiverse Spider-Man concept before Into the Spider-Verse.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1997 solo series for Maverick (Christopher Nord), the mercenary mutant with carbonadium absorption powers from Wolverine's past in Team X. A competent but unremarkable character vehicle that explored Nord's complicated loyalties.
author: Jorge Gonzalez

subject: series
synopsis: Jean Graton's Belgian racing car comics series following champion driver Michel Vaillant through spectacular international racing competitions and corporate intrigue. A landmark of European sports adventure comics, meticulous in its automotive detail.
author: Jean Graton

subject: series
synopsis: Yoshiyuki Tomino and Yasuhiko Yoshikazu's manga retelling of the original Gundam anime is the definitive version of the story — richer characterization, more complex politics, and extraordinary mechanical design.
author: Yoshiyuki Tomino, Yoshikazu Yasuhiko

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2002 anthology series featuring stories about everyday mutants who aren't X-Men — ordinary people dealing with extraordinary mutations in the context of a prejudiced world. A humanizing counterpoint to the superheroic X-Men narrative.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marv Wolfman's continuation of the New Teen Titans after the team's name change, running from 1988 to 1996 and spanning some of the title's most ambitious and difficult arcs including the Titans Hunt and the death and return of major characters. Historically essential as the conclusion of Wolfman's defining run on these characters.
author: Marv Wolfman

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1986 New Universe title featuring a young man who can enter the dreams of others, part of Marvel's ambitious but ultimately failed New Universe imprint that launched following Secret Wars. More interesting as a period artifact than as standalone storytelling.
author: W.D. Bards

subject: series
synopsis: Collected volumes of Robert Kirkman and Lorenzo De Felici's sci-fi thriller following a man staging daily solo rescues from the dimension that consumed part of Philadelphia.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Ethan Sacks's sci-fi elseworlds story transplanting an elderly Peter Quill into a future where the Universal Church of Truth has conquered the galaxy, an effective 'Old Man Logan in space' riff with strong art by Robert Gill.
author: Ethan Sacks

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Krahulik and Jerry Holkins' landmark gaming webcomic, launching in 1998 and growing into one of the most influential web comics ever published. The sharp video game commentary and escalating absurdist humor made it foundational to gaming culture and helped establish the PAX convention ecosystem. At its best it's genuinely brilliant satire of the game industry.
author: Jerry Holkins

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1985 Star Comics all-ages series about a young boy searching the universe for his parents, published under Marvel's Star Comics imprint for younger readers. A charming throwback to sci-fi adventure comics in the Saturday morning cartoon tradition.
author: Lennie Herman

subject: series
synopsis: Kurtis J. Wiebe and Roc Upchurch's (later Stjepan Sejic's) fantasy comedy following a mercenary squad of four foul-mouthed adventurers — Hannah, Violet, Dee, and Betty — as they navigate quests, bar fights, and personal drama in a D&D-inspired fantasy world.
author: Kurtis J. Wiebe

subject: series
synopsis: Mao Nanami's romance manga about Hikaru Tsutsui, an otaku convinced he can never attract a 'real' girlfriend, who begins a tentative relationship with Iroha Igarashi, a popular girl with a complicated past. A gentle, character-driven romance that takes its socially awkward protagonist's journey seriously.
author: Mao Nanami

subject: series
synopsis: Masahiko Takajo and Tetsuya Saruwatari's ultra-violent prison manga follows Riki-Oh Saiga, a man with superhuman strength serving time in a privatized prison run by sadistic criminals. Famous for the notoriously gruesome live-action Hong Kong film adaptation.
author: Masahiko Takajo

subject: series
synopsis: Meredith Finch and Ig Guara's epic fantasy series about the last Guardian — a young woman named Rose — and her bonded monster, fighting to save a world enslaved by a dark queen who destroyed all other Guardians.
author: Meredith Finch

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas and Rich Buckler's 1988 twelve-issue series retelling Namor's complete history in updated form. Essential mythology-building for one of Marvel's oldest characters.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: A crime spin-off from the Spawn universe following detectives Sam Burke and Twitch Williams, the two best-written supporting characters from Spawn, as they investigate supernatural murder cases in New York City.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1996 series by Len Kaminski about a band of young monsters — a werewolf, a vampire, a reptile creature — who form a rock band as a cover for their survival in a world that wants to capture or exploit them. A fun concept undercut by inconsistent execution.
author: Len Kaminski

subject: series
synopsis: Sheldon Mayer's semi-autobiographical 1940s DC series about Scribbly Jibbet, a boy cartoonist trying to break into the newspaper comics business, based on Mayer's own early career. A warm, genuinely funny strip that captures the New York comics scene of the 1940s with inside-baseball humor and real affection for its aspirational young protagonist.
author: Sheldon Mayer

synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's paranoid event revealing Skrulls had been secretly replacing Marvel heroes for years, built up through his New Avengers run. Effective as a thriller despite a rushed conclusion, with strong art by Leinil Francis Yu.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

synopsis: Marvel's digital-first Infinity Comic series presenting She-Hulk's legal adventures in the infinite-canvas format, adapting the character's celebrated lawyer-superhero premise for the vertical-scroll reading experience of Marvel Unlimited.
author: Various

synopsis: DC's 1994 installment in the anthology tryout series, featuring short stories spotlighting Huntress, Gunfire, Hitman (in a notable early appearance), and other characters. Hitman's debut here by Garth Ennis and John McCrea is the most historically significant story in the series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak's series following Skaar, the Hulk's savage son born on Sakaar, developing his own mythology before eventually crossing over with his father on Earth. An effective extension of Planet Hulk's world.
author: Greg Pak

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinite Comics digital series featuring Slapstick, the cartoonish dimension-hopping hero, in adventures formatted for the vertical digital reading experience.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: David Hine's series following Pietro Maximoff stealing Terrigen Crystals to restore depowered mutants after House of M, a character study of a desperate man whose actions have catastrophic consequences.
author: David Hine

subject: series
synopsis: Hardcover collections of IDW's Sonic the Hedgehog (2018-), Ian Flynn's post-Archie continuity drawn by Tracy Yardley, Evan Stanley and others.
author: Ian Flynn, Caleb Goellner

synopsis: Isuna Hasekura's manga adaptation follows traveling merchant Kraft Lawrence and Holo, an ancient wolf deity of harvest, as they journey together through a medieval European-inspired world discussing economics, trade, and loneliness. Known for its unusual intelligence and the warmth of its central relationship.
author: Isuna Hasekura

author: Various

author: Joe Brusha, Pat Shand

synopsis: Marvel's 1990 Epic Comics series about a team of mercenaries in near-future America, one of Epic's attempts at a grounded action thriller in the post-Watchmen era.
